$comment: Layer 07 (Agent public state + inbox/queues) direct-primitive canonical shape, discriminated by a top-level `agent_inbox` key -- a fourth schema for conformance/agent/'s own directory (alongside the unified, transform, and tool_registry shapes), not a fifth canonical family: scenarios here exercise the real Inbox primitive directly (steer/follow_up/inject/claim/clear/has_queued_messages), not a full agent-loop turn. No provider, no tool, no run-loop timing.

expect.$comment: Maps each action's own `observe` name to its expected value. Every `observe` name used in `actions` must have exactly one entry here, and vice versa -- checked by the runner, not merely by convention.

action.$comment: L07-R004 (second independent Rust review): `minProperties: 1` alone let an action carry more than one operation key at once (e.g. both `steer` and `follow_up`), which no runner semantics defines an order for. `oneOf` on `required` makes exactly one operation key mandatory -- a document naming two operation keys matches more than one branch and is rejected; a document naming zero matches none and is also rejected. `observe` is additionally constrained to the two operations that actually have a pinned-Pi return value to observe (`claim`/`has_queued_messages`): the four enqueue/clear branches also forbid `observe` via `not: {required: ["observe"]}`, so an action combining e.g. `steer` with `observe` matches zero branches and is rejected, not silently accepted the way the `properties` list alone (which only names it as a valid key somewhere) would allow.

observe.description: Names this action's own observable result for the `expect` map. Only meaningful on `claim`/`has_queued_messages`; enqueue/clear actions never carry one, since they have no pinned-Pi return value to observe.

text.description: A plain UserMessage(text) is sufficient to prove ordering/independence; the accepted-message-domain rule itself (AG-011) is proven by Python/Rust language tests, not this schema, to avoid encoding host-specific message-variant tagging here.
